newsitem.title: USA: DuPont executives meet with Yeltsin rival.
newsitem.headline: DuPont executives meet with Yeltsin rival.

text.p: General Alexander Lebed, a political rival of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, on Tuesday met with DuPont Co executives in Delaware.
A DuPont spokeswoman told Reuters that Lebed met for an hour with DuPont Chief Executive Jack Krol and the chairman of DuPont Europe, Jerry Blumberg.
Lebed stopped in Wilmington while en route to New York after the inauguration of President Bill Clinton in Washington on Monday.

According to Kathy Forte of DuPont, it was an unofficial courtesy visit initiated by the general, who opposed Yeltsin in last year's presidential election, only to become one of his advisers for a brief time after the ballot.

"He wanted to provide insights regarding the general climate for private investment in Russia. Russia is an important country for Dupont's growth. We have offices in Moscow and have established a business presence in Russia for a number of our businesses," she said.
